questions.q: Why does the young white man return to Mrs Lithebe's?
choices: To apologise for his angry words and to talk about getting a lawyer
To take Kumalo to the prison
questions.explain: 'When my work goes wrong, I hurt myself and I hurt others also. But then I grow ashamed, and that is why I am here.'

questions.q: Why does the young man say Kumalo should have a lawyer?
choices: Because the truth must be hidden
Not because the truth must not be told, but because 'I do not trust your brother' — John plans to deny Matthew and the third man were there
questions.explain: A lawyer would also know how to make the court believe Absalom fired 'because he was afraid', with no intention to kill.

questions.q: What defence does Father Vincent say the lawyer will run?
choices: The plain truth — that the shot was fired in fear and not to kill
questions.explain: 'It is to be the truth, and nothing but the truth, and indeed, the man I am thinking of would not otherwise take the case.'

questions.q: What does Father Vincent say about sorrow and fear?
choices: 'Sorrow is better than fear. For fear impoverishes always, while sorrow may enrich.'
questions.explain: 'Fear is a journey, a terrible journey, but sorrow is at least an arriving.'

questions.q: What image does Father Vincent use for what a man can do after disaster?
choices: 'About a storm he can do nothing, but he can rebuild a house'
Wait for the storm to pass
questions.explain: He speaks 'in that symbolic language that is like the Zulu tongue.'

questions.q: When Father Vincent mentions 'a thief upon the cross', how does Kumalo answer sharply?
choices: 'My son was not a thief' — and he insists the murdered man was 'a good man... devoted to our people'
'The thief was forgiven, so is my son.'
'Do not speak of the Bible to me.'
questions.explain: Kumalo calls it 'the greatest evil I have known.'

questions.q: What does Kumalo say he sees in his son that grieves him most?
choices: 'I see no shame in him, no pity for those he has hurt' — the boy seems to weep only for himself, for his danger
questions.explain: 'Can a person lose all sense of evil? A boy, brought up as he was brought up?'

questions.q: What does Father Vincent tell Kumalo NOT to pray for?
choices: For himself, and to understand the ways of God
The soul of the murdered man
questions.explain: 'For they are secret. Who knows what life is? — for life is a secret.'

questions.q: For whom does Father Vincent tell Kumalo to pray?
choices: Gertrude and her child, the girl, the grandchild, the bereaved wife and children, the soul of the man who was killed, and all white people 'who would do justice if they were not afraid'
questions.explain: 'And give thanks where you can give thanks. For nothing is better.'

questions.q: How does Kumalo react when he learns the lawyer will take the case 'pro deo'?
choices: He is suspicious of the offer
He stammers, 'I have never met such kindness', and turns away his face because 'he wept easily in these days'
questions.explain: 'Pro deo' means 'for God' — the case is taken for nothing, or almost nothing.
